clue.text: See an island reminding one of Madeira?

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced 'see', a standard crossword equivalence
a key (or cay) is a low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Someone spots an island that brings Madeira to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeira looks like the Portuguese island, which makes 'an island' seem part of the picture; but the Madeira meant is the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira cake is a plain sponge, so something reminiscent of it has a cake-like texture or flavour.

clue.text: The enrobing bishop is, in short, a shirker

indicators.note: the dressed-up bishop group is placed inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: to enrobe is to dress in a robe, so these letters wrap around the bishop's letter

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A robed bishop is called, briefly, a slacker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' reads as 'briefly', but 'short' is the outer word and 'is in' the insertion signal. St Cuthbert was himself a bishop, of Lindisfarne, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuthbert was First World War British slang for a man thought to be dodging military service, hence any shirker.

clue.text: Port and the smallest amount of cumin introduced to dish

indicators.note: one letter is put into the dish word, as a spice is put into food

parts.note: a karahi is the deep two-handled pan used in Indian and Pakistani cooking

indicators.note: only a single letter, the first, of cumin is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe: add a pinch of cumin to the dish, with port to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink in a cooking scene; it is the definition, a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city and its chief seaport on the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Be very involved with sell-out — we can't ask for more than this

definitions.text: we can't ask for more than this

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Getting deeply caught up in a sell-out show is the most anyone could hope for.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your level best means trying as hard as you possibly can, the utmost effort anyone could demand.

clue.text: Odd risk to run over a way to move timber

indicators.note: the letters run about and spill over the A, being rearranged together

explanation.surface: An unusual danger of running over a logging track.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ODD RISK takes in the A from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid road was a track of greased logs along which felled lumber was dragged in North American logging.

clue.text: Knowledge principally within reach of Earth, go seeking adventure

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so the first letter of knowledge is taken

parts.note: nigh means near, close at hand
Terran, from Latin terra, means belonging to the planet Earth, a science-fiction usage
a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: With knowledge and Earth close by, set out to look for adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Knight-errantry is the practice of medieval knights who roamed in search of chivalrous exploits.

clue.text: Avoided transporting Engels or Nietzsche, both in the end lacking fare

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter
transporting means carrying, so the philosophers' first name is carried inside the word for avoided

parts.note: to dodge or avoid it
both Engels and Nietzsche had the first name Friedrich

explanation.surface: Someone dodged carrying two German thinkers, both of whom went hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: DUCKED carries FRIEDRICH; then both DUCKED and FRIEDRICH drop their last letters (D and H). 'Fare' means food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck fried rice is a Chinese takeaway dish, so it is food, which is one sense of fare.

clue.text: Disregarded spare tool

parts.note: over means left over, surplus, spare
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone ignored a spare tool.
explanation.walkthrough: To oversee once meant to overlook in the sense of failing to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversaw in its old sense of overlooked means failed to notice or ignored.

clue.text: African city medic has alias

indicators.note: the doctor's letters hold the alias inside them, as one has something

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
AKA, 'also known as', introduces an alias

explanation.surface: A doctor in an African city goes by another name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dakar is the capital of Senegal, on the West African coast.

clue.text: We can't decide on remote French retailers we patronise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: television viewers who keep switching channels with the remote control
second meaning: Britons who cross the English Channel to shop in France

explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' looks like an adjective (distant), but it is the TV remote control.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping between channels describes both restless TV viewers and day-trippers crossing the English Channel for cheap shopping.

clue.text: Connected cast to the audience

indicators.note: what an audience receives is heard, so the word for cast is said aloud

parts.note: threw is the past tense of throw, to cast

explanation.surface: An actor's company were linked to the people watching.
explanation.definitionFit: On a telephone, being put through means being connected to the person you called.

clue.text: Unable to resist Scottish Isle? (It's annoying having to share hotel)

indicators.note: two words with a common letter overlap, so that letter appears only once

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
'heck!' is an exclamation of annoyance
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Couldn't resist a Scottish island trip, though sharing a hotel was a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH ends and HECK begins with the hotel letter, so the two words overlap on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in check means restrained or kept under control, so unable to break free.

clue.text: A number of the Beatles controversially snub heartsick fans

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so these letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: The band, controversially, cold-shoulders their lovesick followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' looks like the Beatles' admirers but is a verb signalling the anagram. The 1968 song was controversial, read by some as pro-Soviet.
explanation.definitionFit: Back in the USSR is the opening track of the 1968 'White Album', a song by the Beatles.

It's a surprise they are up over the optics

definitions.text: It's a surprise they are up over the optics

parts.words: It's a surprise they are up over the optics
parts.note: figuratively a reaction of surprise; literally hairs lifted above the eyes

explanation.walkthrough: Optics is slang for eyes; the phrase is both a show of surprise and a literal description of brows lifted above them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the hairy arches above the eyes is the classic facial expression of astonishment or disapproval.

clue.text: No longer concerned with maintaining a favourable image, moves on man-eaters

indicators.text: No longer concerned with maintaining a favourable image
indicators.note: image management is public relations, so its abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: to progress is to move on or advance
PR stands for public relations

explanation.surface: Having stopped caring about how they look, the man-eaters press ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales a female ogre devours humans, so these monsters are literal man-eaters.

clue.text: Artist's device which is shifty the forger's in on?

indicators.note: shifty letters shift about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what dodgy painting trick a forger is in on.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes the S of 'forger's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreshortening is the drawing technique of compressing an object's depth to give the illusion of perspective.

clue.text: Only child we hear Elgar's worked on close up

parts.note: OC is an abbreviation for only child

indicators.note: the word that follows is to be heard as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: Elgar, the setter, has clued this puzzle: put together its clues

explanation.surface: Only child Elgar's work is finished close by, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar is the composer in the surface, but here the setter of this puzzle, who has clued it.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or shut off, as an occluded artery is closed up.

clue.text: Cop fired after politician forged sanction

indicators.note: forged means fashioned or faked, so the letters are reshaped
fired means dismissed, so those letters are thrown out of the mix

explanation.surface: A police officer was sacked after a politician faked approval.
explanation.walkthrough: Take C, O and P out of POLITICIAN and rearrange what is left (LITIIAN).
explanation.definitionFit: To initial a document is to sign it with your initials as approval or authorisation.

clue.text: The common origin of Cinderella and Snow White?

definitions.text: The common origin of Cinderella and Snow White?

parts.words: The common origin of Cinderella and Snow White?
parts.note: both fairy tales start with the same stock opening words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Origin' seems to ask about history or sources, but it means the literal opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional fairy stories conventionally begin with this formula, so it is where both tales start.

clue.text: Inception filmed here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a beginning or start
second meaning: read as two words, the place where a film is shot

explanation.walkthrough: Inception is also the title of a Christopher Nolan film, which ties the two readings together.
explanation.definitionFit: The onset of something is its beginning, and a film scene is shot on the studio set.

clue.text: See 22
See 22
See 3

ZZ Top from early on slide after double shaving maybe?

indicators.note: the shaved letter comes after the slide
the early letter goes on after the rest

parts.note: shute is a variant spelling of chute, a slide

indicators.note: the word is shaved at both ends twice, leaving only its central letter
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something about the band ZZ Top, early on, sliding after a double shave.
explanation.walkthrough: ZZ Top are a bearded rock band, so shaving fits; but ZZ alone is the definition, the cartoon sign of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Zs drawn in a comic signify snoring, and shut-eye is informal for sleep.

clue.text: Ultimately son not good in producing dried fruit

indicators.note: at the very end of the word, where the swap is made
one letter is put in place of the other, son instead of good

parts.note: raising crops or animals is producing them
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: In the end the son was no good at making dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are grapes that have been dried.

clue.text: Written work about doing daily series when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the final letter round to the front

parts.note: re means about or concerning
at means doing, as in 'hard at it'
the i is a British daily newspaper
a set is a series or group

explanation.surface: An essay on doing a daily series while cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, AT, I and SET make REATISET; 'when cycling' moves the last T to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal, extended piece of writing on a single subject.

clue.text: This sexologist would be awfully unpleasant in hospitals

indicators.note: the clue says the name would sit in the hospital letters to make the longer word, so those letters are stripped away

parts.note: hellish means dreadful, awfully unpleasant
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital; two hospitals give two of them

explanation.surface: A sex researcher would be most unwelcome in hospitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written backwards: the name, put in two Hs, would make HELLISH, so take the Hs out of HELLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Havelock Ellis was a pioneering British writer on human sexuality around 1900.
